A messy experiment export

Source: R/data.R
messy_export.Rd

The raw export of a lexical decision experiment with 24 participants run in two labs, as it might come out of experiment software and a spreadsheet. The underlying data are clean (high- vs low-frequency words, as in rt_frequency); the export needs cleaning before analysis. All columns except Item are character, so this data set is the exception to the package's factor convention.

Usage

messy_export

Format

A tibble with 1086 rows and 10 columns:

Subject ID

Participant ID, written in four ways (P01, p1, P 01, 01).

Lab

"A" or "B".

Age

Age, sometimes with " years".

Block

"practice" or "test".

Item

Item number, 1 to 40; practice items reuse 1 to 4.

Cond.

Word frequency, spelled in eight ways (high, High, HIGH , hi, low, Low, LOW, lo ), some with trailing spaces.

Response Time (ms)

Reaction time, with a decimal comma in lab B, "-999" or "" for missing values.

ACC

Accuracy: "1"/"0" in lab A, "correct"/"incorrect" in lab B.

Timestamp

Time of the trial: 2026-05-04 10:00:03 in lab A, 04.05.2026 10:00 in lab B.

Notes

Always empty.

Source

data-raw/messy_export.R

Details

Problems to fix: inconsistent IDs, condition labels and accuracy codes; a decimal comma; two codes for missing values; ages stored as text; two date formats; 96 practice trials; 30 duplicated test trials; an empty column; column names with spaces and punctuation. True model of the clean data: log(rt) = 6.38 + 0.1 * low + p0 + w0 + e, with participant (SD 0.12) and item (SD 0.05) effects and residual SD 0.15; accuracy is 96% for high- and 88% for low-frequency words.

Examples

x <- messy_export
table(x$Cond.)
#> 
#> HIGH   High   LOW   Low    hi  high   lo    low 
#>   128   131   132   135   138   142   142   138 
condition <- ifelse(substr(tolower(trimws(x$Cond.)), 1, 1) == "h", "high", "low")
rt <- as.numeric(sub(",", ".", x[["Response Time (ms)"]]))
rt[rt == -999] <- NA
id <- as.integer(gsub("[^0-9]", "", x[["Subject ID"]]))
test <- x$Block == "test" & !duplicated(data.frame(id, x$Item, x$Block))
tapply(rt[test], condition[test], mean, na.rm = TRUE)
#>     high      low 
#> 592.8893 631.4163
